goldenPoints: Cherry-red postmortem lividity = carbon monoxide poisoning
Pelvis is the most reliable bone for sex determination; skull is second
Tattooing without blackening or burning = shot fired from intermediate (close) range, not contact
Judicial hanging kills by C2–C3 fracture-dislocation, not asphyxia
IPC 304A = death by negligence; IPC 320 = grievous hurt; IPC 84 = McNaughten insanity defence
Dowry death (within 7 years of marriage) and custodial death require a Magistrate's inquest
MTP: 1 RMP up to 20 weeks, 2 RMPs from 20–24 weeks in specified categories, Medical Board beyond 24 weeks
Atropine is the mainstay of organophosphorus poisoning; gastric lavage is contraindicated in corrosive and kerosene poisoning
Fine tenacious froth at the nose and mouth is the hallmark of antemortem drowning
Barberio's test — yellow needle-shaped spermine picrate crystals — confirms semen
intro: Forensic Medicine carries 10 questions in every FMGE paper and is one of the highest-scoring subjects per hour of study: the stems repeat classic textbook facts — IPC sections, inquest rules, rigor and lividity timings, firearm wound ranges, and toxicology antidotes. Learn the numbers and named signs cold; there is very little conceptual depth to hide behind.
subject: Forensic Medicine
tagline: FMGE asks law sections, postmortem changes, injury patterns and poison antidotes — almost all one-line facts

topics.askedAs: PM change timings, lividity colours, decomposition order
topics.oneLiner: Cherry-red lividity = CO poisoning; green over the right iliac fossa starts putrefaction; prostate and uterus putrefy last.
points: Livor mortis (postmortem staining) appears in 1–3 hours, blanches on pressure early, and gets fixed in about 6–12 hours
Cherry-red postmortem lividity is the classic sign of carbon monoxide poisoning
Rigor mortis starts in 1–2 hours, completes by 6–12 hours, and passes off in 18–36 hours; it begins earliest in the heart
Cadaveric spasm (instantaneous rigor) occurs at the moment of death under intense stress — the weapon stays gripped in the hand
In starvation deaths, autopsy shows an empty shrunken stomach, a distended gallbladder and loss of body fat
Putrefaction is driven mainly by Clostridium welchii; its first external sign is greenish discoloration over the right iliac fossa (over the caecum), in 12–18 hours in summer
Order of putrefaction of organs: larynx and trachea first; prostate and the non-gravid uterus resist the longest
Adipocere (saponified fat) needs a moist, warm, anaerobic environment and takes a minimum of about 3 weeks to form
Mummification needs dry air and heat; the body shrinks, darkens and is preserved
Casper's dictum: one week of decomposition in air equals two weeks in water and eight weeks buried in earth
topics.title: Postmortem Changes: Lividity, Rigor & Putrefaction
topics.trap: Rigor mortis is NOT instantaneous — stiffness within minutes of death after violent struggle is cadaveric spasm, a different and rarer finding.

topics.askedAs: injury classification from the wound description
topics.oneLiner: Bridging in the depth = laceration; clean-cut structures = incised. Tailing marks where the blade left the skin.
points: Abrasion (graze): superficial injury of epidermis only; heals without a scar
Contusion (bruise): bleeding under intact skin; colour sequence red → blue → green (haemosiderin, ~5–6 days) → yellow → fades in about 2 weeks
Laceration: torn, irregular wound from blunt force, with tissue bridging in its depth; vessels and nerves cross it uncut
Incised wound: length greater than depth, clean margins, tailing at the end; structures in the depth are cut cleanly
A stab (punctured) wound has depth greater than length; a penetrating wound enters a body cavity
Depressed ('pond') fracture of the skull is classically caused by a hammer or similar small, heavy weapon
Defence wounds are seen on the hands, forearms and palms of a victim who tried to ward off or grab the weapon
Hesitation cuts — multiple superficial parallel cuts at the wrist or neck — suggest suicidal intent
topics.title: Mechanical Injuries: Blunt, Sharp & Defence Wounds
topics.trap: A scalp wound from a fall can look incised (split laceration) — check for tissue bridging before calling it a sharp-force injury.

topics.askedAs: range of fire from entry wound; blast injury category
topics.oneLiner: Burning < blackening < tattooing — the furthest sign present fixes the range. In blast: wave = primary, fragments = secondary.
points: Entry wound: margins inverted, surrounded by an abrasion/contusion ring (grease collar)
Exit wound: margins everted, with no burning, blackening or tattooing
Contact shot over bone (skull) gives a stellate (star-shaped) entry wound from gas expanding under the skin
Burning and singeing of hair occur only within a few centimetres; blackening (soot) extends further; unburnt powder tattooing extends furthest
Tattooing present but NO blackening or singeing means a close (intermediate-range) shot, just beyond flame and smoke range
A distant shot leaves only the hole with its abrasion ring — no burning, blackening or tattooing
Calibre of a rifled weapon is measured between two opposite lands of the rifling
Primary blast injury is from the shock wave: tympanic membrane rupture is the most common injury; blast lung is the classic lethal one
Secondary blast injury comes from flying fragments; tertiary from the body being thrown or a structure collapsing on it
topics.title: Firearm & Blast Injuries
topics.trap: Inverted margins mean ENTRY even if the wound looks small; exit wounds are everted and never show tattooing.

topics.askedAs: hanging type and cause of death; drowning signs
topics.oneLiner: Judicial hanging = broken neck (C2–C3); fine froth at the nostrils = antemortem drowning.
points: Hanging: the neck is constricted by a ligature tightened by the weight of the body itself
In partial hanging, even the weight of the head alone can act as the constricting force
Judicial (long-drop) hanging kills by fracture-dislocation of C2–C3 vertebrae (hangman's fracture), not by asphyxia
Throttling is manual strangulation; smothering occludes the nose and mouth — look for facial congestion, petechiae and lip bruising
Petechial haemorrhages (Tardieu spots) appear above the level of constriction in asphyxial deaths
Fine, tenacious, white froth at the nose and mouth is the most characteristic external sign of antemortem drowning
Washerwoman's hands and feet (wrinkled, bleached palms and soles) are immersion signs, not proof of drowning
Lungs in wet drowning are ballooned (emphysema aquosum) and show Paltauf's haemorrhages under the pleura
Water and debris deep in the airways and stomach, and diatoms in bone marrow matching the water, support antemortem drowning
Dry drowning is death from laryngospasm with little water entering the lungs
topics.title: Asphyxia: Hanging, Strangulation & Drowning
topics.trap: Immersion signs occur in any body lying in water — they never by themselves prove drowning; and partial hanging needs only head weight, so it is still hanging, not strangulation.

topics.askedAs: sex, race and identity from bones and remains
topics.oneLiner: Pelvis first for sex; cephalic index 85 = brachycephalic; lymph nodes betray the vanished tattoo.
points: The pelvis is the single most reliable bone for sex determination; the skull is the next best
Female pelvis: broad and shallow, subpubic angle >90°, round/oval brim; male pelvis is narrow with a heart-shaped brim
Cephalic index = (maximum skull breadth / maximum length) × 100; above 80 is brachycephalic (short, broad skull)
Cephalic index 85 indicates a brachycephalic skull, classically of Mongoloid race; dolichocephalic (<75) is seen in Negroid/Aryan groups
Superimposition matches a recovered skull with a photograph of the suspected person
A tattoo invisible on a decomposed body can be proved by finding its pigment in the regional lymph nodes
Gustafson's method estimates age from six secondary changes in a tooth, including root transparency
The precipitin test distinguishes human blood and bone from animal — used to prove remains are human
Barr bodies (sex chromatin) in buccal cells indicate a chromosomally female pattern
The medial end of the clavicle is the last epiphysis to fuse, around 21–25 years
topics.title: Identification of the Dead & the Living
topics.trap: Do not pick the skull as the best bone for sex — the pelvis beats it; the skull is only second best.

topics.askedAs: the section number for a legal situation
topics.oneLiner: 304A negligence, 304B dowry death, 320 grievous hurt, 84 McNaughten — the four numbers FMGE repeats.
points: Criminal medical negligence was classically IPC 304A — death by a rash or negligent act (carried into the BNS; FMGE PYQs still frame it as 304A)
Dowry death is IPC 304B: death of a woman within 7 years of marriage with dowry-related cruelty; the inquest is by a Magistrate
Cruelty by a husband or his relatives for dowry: IPC 498A
Hurt is IPC 319; grievous hurt is IPC 320 — its list includes fracture, permanent disfiguration, and hurt endangering life
Culpable homicide is IPC 299; murder is IPC 300
Causing miscarriage without the woman's consent: IPC 313
A doctor acting in good faith with valid consent is protected by IPC 88; emergency care without consent by IPC 92
Consent of a child under 12 years or of an insane person is invalid — IPC 90
McNaughten rule (IPC 84): the insanity defence — the accused could not know the nature of the act, or that it was wrong or contrary to law
Only the President (Article 72) and the Governor (Article 161) can pardon or commute a death sentence
topics.title: Medical Law: IPC Sections FMGE Loves
topics.trap: Grievous hurt needs the IPC 320 list — a simple fracture IS grievous hurt, even if the patient recovers fully.

topics.askedAs: who conducts the inquest; witness and summons rules
topics.oneLiner: Dowry death and custodial death = Magistrate's inquest; a criminal summons always beats a civil one.
points: Police inquest (CrPC 174) is the commonest inquest in India, conducted by the investigating police officer
Magistrate's inquest (CrPC 176) is mandatory for dowry death, death in police custody or prison, and for exhumation
Death of a married woman within 7 years in suspicious circumstances goes to a Magistrate's inquest, not a police inquest alone
A coroner's inquest survives only in Mumbai
A criminal summons takes priority over a civil summons for the same day
A common (ordinary) witness testifies to facts seen or heard; an expert witness gives opinion evidence
In the witness box, a doctor is usually both — common witness for the findings, expert for the opinion
Leading questions are allowed in cross-examination, not in examination-in-chief (except by the court's permission)
Dying declaration: preferably recorded by a Magistrate, but one recorded by a doctor or police officer is valid; the doctor must certify the patient is compos mentis; no oath is given
Perjury (false evidence) is punishable under IPC 191–193
topics.title: Inquest, Courts & Medical Evidence
topics.trap: A dying declaration does NOT need a Magistrate to be valid — doctor-recorded, with a fitness (compos mentis) certificate, is admissible.

topics.askedAs: MTP week limits, consent, banned tests
topics.oneLiner: 20 weeks = 1 doctor, 20–24 = 2 doctors + special category, beyond 24 = Medical Board for fetal anomaly.
points: MTP Act 1971 (amended 2021): termination up to 20 weeks needs the opinion of ONE registered medical practitioner
From 20 to 24 weeks: opinion of TWO RMPs, and only for specified categories of women (rape survivors, minors, change of marital status, disabilities, fetal anomalies, humanitarian settings)
Beyond 24 weeks: only for substantial fetal abnormalities, decided by a state-level Medical Board
There is no week limit when termination is immediately necessary to save the woman's life
Consent: an adult woman's own consent suffices; for a minor or a mentally ill woman, written consent of the guardian is required
Pregnancy resulting from rape is a legal ground — the anguish is presumed to be a grave injury to mental health
MTP by an unqualified person or at an unapproved place is punishable under the Act
The two-finger (per-vaginum) test in rape examination is banned by the Supreme Court — unscientific and violative of dignity
Excessive sexual desire in a man is satyriasis; in a woman, nymphomania
Semen and other biological evidence in sexual offence cases is preserved dry, never in formalin
topics.title: MTP Act & Sexual Jurisprudence
topics.trap: For a mentally ill adult woman, MTP consent must come from her guardian — her own consent alone does not satisfy the Act.

topics.askedAs: poison from the smell/signs; antidote choice
topics.oneLiner: SLUDGE + garlic smell + small pupils = organophosphorus → atropine first, oxime early; never lavage a corrosive.
points: Organophosphorus poisoning: salivation, lacrimation, diarrhoea, miosis and bradycardia (SLUDGE picture), garlic odour, and a fall in plasma cholinesterase
Atropine is the mainstay of OP poisoning; pralidoxime reactivates cholinesterase if given early
In pure carbamate poisoning atropine is used but oximes are avoided
Aluminium phosphide (Celphos) releases phosphine; there is no specific antidote, and refractory shock with myocarditis kills
Gastric lavage is contraindicated in corrosive (acid/alkali) poisoning and in kerosene or hydrocarbon ingestion
Activated charcoal poorly adsorbs iron, lithium, alcohols, corrosives and hydrocarbons
Paraquat causes pulmonary fibrosis and multi-organ failure; even a small dose can be fatal
Body packer syndrome: a courier who swallows drug packets — abdominal X-ray shows the packets; laxatives and an enema kit in the luggage are the classic stem clues
topics.title: Toxicology I: Pesticides & Agricultural Poisons
topics.trap: Never do gastric lavage in corrosive or kerosene poisoning — perforation and aspiration make it dangerous.

topics.askedAs: drug from its signature signs; first step in snake bite
topics.oneLiner: Formication + black tongue = cocaine; first aid for snake bite is reassure and immobilise — never incise.
points: Opioid poisoning triad: pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression and coma; naloxone reverses it
Cocaine abuse: tactile hallucinations (formication, 'cocaine bugs' — Magnan's sign), scratch marks, nasal septal perforation and blackish discoloration of the tongue
Cannabis: the most common effect is euphoria, with conjunctival injection and increased appetite
Datura poisoning: dry hot skin, dilated pupils, delirium — 'dry as a bone, blind as a bat, red as a beet, mad as a hen'; antidote is physostigmine
Cardiac glycoside (digitalis) toxicity classically disturbs colour vision — yellow vision (xanthopsia) and coloured halos, with arrhythmias
Blood for alcohol estimation at autopsy is preserved with sodium fluoride, which prevents fermentation
Methanol poisoning causes visual loss ('snow-field' vision) and severe metabolic acidosis; it is treated with ethanol or fomepizole
Arsenic poisoning: rice-water stools, garlic odour of breath, Mees lines on the nails; chelation with BAL or succimer
Sanguinarine in argemone oil (adulterated mustard oil) causes epidemic dropsy — oedema, cardiac failure and glaucoma
Snake bite first aid: reassure the patient, immobilise the limb and rush to hospital — do NOT incise, suck, or apply a tight tourniquet

Krait bite is typically nocturnal and nearly painless with neuroparalytic features; viper bite causes bleeding and local necrosis; anti-snake venom is given for systemic envenomation, not for dry bites
topics.title: Toxicology II: Drugs of Abuse, Metals & Snake Bite
topics.trap: First step in snake bite is reassurance and immobilisation — incision, suction and tourniquets are harmful and always the wrong option.

topics.askedAs: which preservative / which test confirms it
topics.oneLiner: Yellow needles with picric acid = Barberio = semen; salt solution preserves viscera, spirit fails for phenol and phosphorus.
points: Routine viscera preservation uses a saturated solution of common salt
Rectified spirit is NOT used when phenol, phosphorus, alcohol or kerosene poisoning is suspected
Blood for alcohol estimation is collected with sodium fluoride plus potassium oxalate
Barberio's test: picric acid with semen forms yellow, needle-shaped crystals of spermine picrate — it confirms semen
Florence test (iodine reagent) gives dark brown crystals of choline iodide — a screening test for semen
The acid phosphatase test is a sensitive screening test for semen in sexual offence cases
Blood-stained items are air-dried at room temperature and packed in paper — never sealed wet in plastic
Heavy metals such as arsenic and copper persist in hair, nails and bones and can be detected years after death
Exhumation is ordered by a Magistrate and carried out in daylight in the presence of a police officer and a medical officer
topics.title: Specimens, Preservation & Forensic Tests
topics.trap: Formalin is for histopathology specimens, never for toxicology viscera — it ruins chemical analysis.
